text.p: LME copper extended its rally on Tuesday afternoon, but ran into forward selling and profit taking after notching up fresh highs. Many of the other metals marked time, while tin dived after failing to sustain higher numbers.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 0.10 points to 251.30

Three months copper skipped to $2,433 per tonne in inter-office trade after hectic activity on the morning kerb, the highest since early March. Widespread buying was seen, including by funds, traders said. The premium of cash over three months metal was slightly narrower at $53/$56 compared to $60/$65 on Monday.

Aluminium continued to move sideways after last week's gains, ending the day unchanged at $1,670. The market may need further consolidation or even a correction before it can gather enough steam to mount a raid on March highs just above $1,700, analysts said.

Tin lost heart after failing to sustain gains from last week's rally and ended with charts looking shaky again. Prices broke below the 100-day moving average at $5,868 as well as short-term 10 and 30-day averages.
Last business in nickel was also weaker, but not to the extent in tin, finishing down $65 at $7,770.
Lead was moribund, trapped in a narrow range, ending the day $8 softer at $622.
Zinc moved sideways again after last week's sharp move higher, finishing $2 firmer at $1,337.
Alloy ended at $1,523/27, little changed from Monday's $1,520/30.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on the bearish tone linked to USDA's weekly crop condition ratings, traders said. USDA Monday said as of Sunday, the U.S. winter wheat crop rated 53 percent good to excellent, above the 50 percent in that category the previous week. Wheat closed one to five cents per bushel lower, with May down five at $3.88 a bushel. July was 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower at $3.95-1/2.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures recovered from early weakness to close higher Tuesday, as funds covered short positions in gold, and Russian supply disruptions continued to provide support for platinum group metals (PGMs). "Gold prices have now built a base around $340 an ounce this year, with lower prices clearly attracting physical demand," Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt said. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $349.25/75, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $348.90 an ounce, and the New York close Monday around $347.40/90.

June IPE Brent ended the day just a few cents lower on Tuesday as the expected retracement failed to happen. Brokers said many locals had taken short postions early in the day but bought back as the early downward move failed to hold its momentum. "Everyone expected a retracement so the market went lower early but there was no momentum and they lost their bottle and covered themselves. No-body wanted to be short before the API's," one said. June Brent ended Tuesday down some nine cents at $19.63, well off the day's low of $19.44 a barrel. The contract, which expires on Thursday, gained almost 80 cents on Monday.
